answer: A stake-bonded identity registry makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can transact, so spawning a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits, like trying to fill a canyon with sable sand one grain at a time. Honest agents earn their bond back plus fees, while detected fakes lose it. A small grove of verified agents can then vouch for newcomers only by risking part of their own stake, so trust grows through real capital at risk rather than free account creation.
